argv:
You generate synthetic meeting transcripts with gold annotations for LiveMinutes, a research dataset modeled on the AMI Meeting Corpus scenario meetings.

In AMI scenario meetings, a team of four plays a design team in a fictional company. The roles are Project Manager (PM), Marketing Expert (ME), User Interface designer (UI) and Industrial Designer (ID). A series has four meetings: (a) kickoff, (b) functional design, (c) conceptual design, (d) detailed design. Later meetings refer back to earlier ones.

Write natural spoken conversation the way AMI transcripts read: short turns, fillers ("um", "uh", "yeah"), backchannels ("mm-hmm", "okay"), interruptions, people building on each other, and some disfluency. Do not write a screenplay. Do not narrate. No stage directions.

Each segment is one dialogue-act-like unit: one speaker, usually one clause or short sentence, sometimes just a backchannel. Give each segment an AMI dialogue-act type from this set:
  bck backchannel, stl stall, fra fragment, inf inform, sug suggest, ass assess,
  el.inf elicit-inform, el.sug elicit-offer-or-suggestion, el.ass elicit-assessment,
  el.und elicit-comment-understanding, off offer, und comment-about-understanding,
  be.pos be-positive, be.neg be-negative, oth other

Absent participants NEVER speak. Speaker labels are ground truth: use only the labels you are given.

The gold annotations must be exactly true of the transcript you write. Refer to segments by their "n" number. Every number you cite must exist.

Output a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown fences.

request.user:
Write meeting SY0104b: meeting "b" (functional design) of series SY0104.

PROJECT
The team is designing a reusable coffee cup with a deposit system.

PARTICIPANTS (label, role, status for this meeting)
A  Marketing Expert (ME)  Priya  present
B  Project Manager (PM)  Tom  present
C  Industrial Designer (ID)  Lena  present
D  User Interface designer (UI)  Marco  present

EARLIER MEETINGS IN THIS SERIES
Stay consistent with them. Refer back to them, follow up on their open action items, and keep the same product and team.

[SY0104a, kickoff]
  abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting and noted that the marketing expert was absent because she was attending a packaging trade fair in Hamburg. The team members introduced themselves, and the project manager presented the brief: a reusable coffee cup with a deposit system aimed at café chains, where cups can be returned at any shop in the scheme, with a target production cost under three euros per cup including the lid. On the deposit system, the user interface designer suggested a simple cash deposit, a return machine, and an optional app with a QR code on the cup to track cups. The team agreed to start with over-the-counter returns, where the barista takes the cup back and refunds the deposit. The deposit amount was not fixed, since it was considered a market question for the marketing expert, and the app idea was left open after the industrial designer raised concerns about cost and about customers who do not want an app. On the cup itself, the industrial designer compared polypropylene with bamboo fibre, noting concerns about the melamine binder used in bamboo fibre cups with hot drinks, and leaned towards polypropylene. The cup must survive commercial dishwashers. The team agreed on a fully separate lid for hygiene and on a single cup size for now, so cups stack and returns stay simple, with the question of multiple sizes to be checked with the marketing expert. The team discussed what to pass on to the absent marketing expert, and the project manager will brief her on her tasks and on the open sizing questions.
  decisions: The cup is aimed at café chains, with returns possible at any café in the scheme. Returns will start as over-the-counter: the barista takes the cup back and refunds the deposit. The cup will have a fully separate, detachable lid rather than a hinged one. The cup will come in one size for now. The deposit amount will not be fixed in this meeting and is left to the marketing expert's research.
  actions: The industrial designer will research cup materials (polypropylene versus bamboo fibre), including heat and commercial dishwasher durability. The user interface designer will map the customer return flow (handing back the cup at the counter, refund). The marketing expert (absent) is assigned to research the deposit amount and existing competitor deposit schemes; the competitor research was first given to the user interface designer and then moved to her. The project manager will send the marketing expert the minutes and the task list, including the one-size idea and the question of whether cafés want different sizes, and will talk to her when she returns on Thursday. The app/QR-code tracking idea is to be revisited at the next meeting.
  problems: The deposit amount is still open, with one or two euros mentioned as amounts used by existing schemes. Whether to use an app with QR-code tracking is unresolved, with the user interface designer in favour and the industrial designer concerned about cost and about excluding customers without the app. The choice between polypropylene and bamboo fibre is pending the industrial designer's research. Whether cafés will want several cup sizes is open and needs market input. The production cost target of under three euros per cup including lid is tight.
  action item SY0104a.ai1: Research cup materials (polypropylene vs bamboo fibre), including heat resistance and commercial dishwasher durability. (owner C, active)
  action item SY0104a.ai2: Build a rough mock-up of the cup shape. (owner C, dropped)
  action item SY0104a.ai3: Map the customer-side return flow (handing the cup back at the counter, refund). (owner D, active)
  action item SY0104a.ai4: Research existing competitor deposit schemes. (owner A, reassigned)
  action item SY0104a.ai5: Research what the deposit amount should be. (owner A, active)
  action item SY0104a.ai6: Send the absent marketing expert the minutes and task list tonight, including the one-size idea and the question of café size preferences, and talk to her when she is back on Thursday. (owner B, active)
  action item SY0104a.ai7: Revisit the app/QR-code cup tracking idea at the next meeting. (owner no owner, active)
  fact (absence): The marketing expert (Priya) was absent because she was at a packaging trade fair in Hamburg.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested a return machine like supermarket bottle machines; the industrial designer considered it too expensive for small cafés.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer proposed an optional app with a QR code on the cup to track cups; the industrial designer objected and it was left open.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): A deposit of one euro was mentioned but not adopted; the deposit amount was left open.
  fact (action_item_removed): The industrial designer's offer to build a rough cup mock-up was dropped as too early.
  fact (plan_change): Competitor deposit scheme research was first given to the user interface designer and then reassigned to the marketing expert.

EDGE CASES THIS MEETING MUST CONTAIN
Weave each one naturally into the project discussion. Each must be clearly present, and each must be tagged with the segments where it happens.
- F1_SARCASM_AS_FACT [F1]: Someone makes a joke or sarcastic remark phrased as a statement of fact (e.g. "great, so we'll just make it out of solid gold"), and the team does not adopt it. The gold summary must NOT report the joke as a decision or fact.
  Required gold labels: summary, edge_cases.
- F1_PLAN_CHANGE [F1]: The team agrees on a plan early in the meeting, then later in the same meeting changes it (different choice, date, or approach). The gold summary must state only the FINAL plan, and may mention that it was revised.
  Required gold labels: summary, edge_cases.

LENGTH
Between 90 and 140 segments.

GOLD LABELS
- summary: AMI-style abstractive summary in third person, using role names ("The project manager ..."). Sections: abstract (3-6 sentences), actions, decisions, problems (open issues). It reflects the meeting's FINAL state: corrected values, final plans, and no jokes or tangents reported as content.
- action_items: every task arising in the meeting. owner is the speaker label of the FINAL owner, and may be an absent participant. owner is null ONLY for a task nobody takes, with owner_unclear true. status is the final status: active, reassigned (owner changed; previous_owners lists earlier owners) or dropped. history lists the events in order. evidence_segments lists the supporting segments.
- qa_facts: atomic facts someone could later ask about ("Who was asked to ...?", "Did the team agree on ...?"). Include every decision (agreed true), every proposal nobody agreed to (type unagreed_proposal, agreed false), action items, removed action items, absences, and plan changes. Because this meeting follows earlier ones, include at least one fact of type reference_to_prior_meeting, with refers_to_meeting set, at a point where someone refers back to an earlier meeting. Do NOT write questions.
- edge_cases: one entry per edge case above, with its scenario_id and the segment numbers that contain it.

OUTPUT JSON SHAPE
{
  "segments": [{"n": 1, "speaker": "A", "da_type": "inf", "text": "..."}],
  "summary": {"abstract": ["..."], "actions": ["..."], "decisions": ["..."], "problems": ["..."]},
  "action_items": [{"n": 1, "description": "...", "owner": "C", "owner_unclear": false, "status": "active", "previous_owners": [], "history": [{"segment": 12, "event": "assigned", "by": "A", "owner": "C"}], "evidence_segments": [12, 13]}],
  "qa_facts": [{"type": "decision", "fact": "...", "agreed": true, "related_action_item": null, "refers_to_meeting": null, "evidence_segments": [40]}],
  "edge_cases": [{"scenario_id": "...", "segments": [20, 21, 22], "note": "one line on how it appears"}]
}
history events: proposed, offered, assigned, accepted, reassigned, dropped, restated. qa_facts types: decision, unagreed_proposal, action_item, action_item_removed, absence, plan_change, reference_to_prior_meeting, other. related_action_item is an action item's "n" or null. refers_to_meeting is an earlier meeting ID of this series or null.
